$comment: The pg_regress baseline (ADR-0001 decision 6): each test of the schedule on the pinned tag, run through the TCP bridge on the build, with --use-existing --max-connections=1. A failed test's normalised diff is regress/diffs/<test>.diff; an unstable test's outcome or diff differed between the recorded runs. `tests` and `summary` are written by `bun run regress --record`; `groups` (why each failing or unstable test fails) are written by hand and kept by --record. `bun run regress` fails on a new failure, a changed diff or a newly unstable test, and reports a vanished failure.

clock-resolution.reason: Unstable. The wasm's wall clock has millisecond resolution (Emscripten's clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME) reads Date.now()), so stats' `stats_reset > <the previous reset>` checks fail whenever two resets fall in the same millisecond. Its diff also carries single-process (no checkpointer, and checkpoint, WAL and I/O counters that do not move as it expects) and session-persistence (temp_buffers after \c).

conversion-modules.reason: The encoding conversion modules in lib/postgresql (utf8_and_*.so, euc_*_and_*.so, latin_and_mic.so, …) import functions pglite.wasm does not export (LocalToUtf, UtfToLocal, report_invalid_encoding, pg_encoding_verifymbchar, …). Calling one throws a TypeError out of the wasm ('resolved is not a function'), which ends the backend: the bridge restarts it and the test loses its connection. opr_sanity gets there by converting through every default conversion, euc_kr through convert_from(…, 'EUC_KR'), copyencoding through client_encoding EUC_JP.

dynamic-loading.reason: libpqwalreceiver.so does not load: it imports WalReceiverFunctions, pg_lsn_in and much of libpq's shared code, which pglite.wasm does not export, so CREATE SUBSCRIPTION … CONNECT fails (object_address, subscription). And once a dlopen has failed, every later one in the backend fails too ('missing magic block') until it restarts: tsearch passes on its own, but here object_address's failed dlopen comes first, and dict_snowball.so no longer loads (tsearch, tsdicts).

extended-protocol-ready.reason: Unstable. An error in an extended-query batch sends a ReadyForQuery before the batch's Sync: pgl_longjmp (overlay pglite/src/pglitec/pglitec.c) sets send_ready_for_query before PostgresMainLongJmp sets ignore_till_sync, and PostgresMainLoopOnce sends it ahead of its next message. psql reports 'message type 0x5a arrived from server while idle' and then pairs results with the wrong queries; where it catches up depends on how the bytes are split between reads, so the diff differs from run to run.

icu-locales.reason: The only ICU collations are und-x-icu and unicode: initdb imports no language locale from the build's ICU data. collate.icu.utf8 skips itself only when there is no ICU collation at all, so it runs and fails on en-x-icu, sv-x-icu, tr-x-icu, ….

regress-library.reason: The tests' C functions are missing (binary_coercible, widget_in, interpt_pp, test_enc_conversion, make_tuple_indirect, trigger_return_old, test_fdw_handler, …), and so is everything built on them (the widget type, the iexit view, the test foreign-data wrapper). The run's --dlpath holds no regress.so: the build tree's own src/test/regress/regress.so imports 21 functions and several data symbols pglite.wasm does not export (IsBinaryCoercible, lseg_intersect, …), so its dlopen fails, and a failed dlopen breaks every later one (see dynamic-loading). Without the file, CREATE FUNCTION … AS :'regresslib' fails with 'could not access file' before any dlopen.

restart-dependent.reason: Unstable. Both load an encoding conversion module after json: whether that dlopen fails ('missing magic block': object_address's failed dlopen breaks every later one until the backend restarts, see dynamic-loading) depends on whether json's stack overflow restarted the backend in between (see wasm-stack). Their diffs also carry other groups' causes: conversion's test functions are in the missing regress library (regress-library); alter_table runs with -O (start-parameters) and shows session-authorization.

session-authorization.reason: RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION does not return to the superuser. Single-user mode (InitializeSessionUserIdStandalone) never gives the session_authorization setting a value, so its reset value is empty and RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION (like SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT) changes nothing: after a test's first SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION, the rest of the test runs as that role, and ownership, privilege and role-management errors follow (and objects the test cannot drop). The bridge's reset sets the superuser back explicitly, so it ends with the test.

session-persistence.reason: psql's \c gets the same backend back: the bridge resets the session instead of starting a new one. Login event triggers never fire (event_trigger_login), temp_buffers cannot be changed once any temporary table was used in the backend (temp, and stats), and plpgsql, loaded by an earlier test, already reserves its prefix (guc, which then also shows session-authorization). temp's PREPARE TRANSACTION also finds prepared transactions disabled: max_prepared_transactions is 0, where pg_regress's own temporary instance sets 2.

single-process.reason: One embedded backend and no other process: no checkpointer, no background or parallel workers. The start parameters set max_worker_processes, max_parallel_workers and max_parallel_workers_per_gather to 0, so plans that expect the default of 2 have no Gather (partition_prune, plpgsql's debug_parallel_query), and select_parallel's own settings launch no worker. stats shows it too (see clock-resolution).

start-parameters.reason: The backend runs with PGlite's start parameters (the driver's START_PARAMS): search_path=public instead of "$user", public shows a table in the role's own schema qualified (create_schema). -O (allow_system_table_mods) also lets alter_table change system catalogs where it expects to be refused (see restart-dependent).

wasm-stack.reason: Deep recursion runs out of the host's native stack before Postgres' max_stack_depth check. check_stack_depth measures the wasm's shadow stack, which holds only the locals whose address is taken, while every wasm frame also takes native stack. infinite_recurse throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded out of the wasm, which ends the backend (the bridge restarts it; the test loses its connection). json and jsonb are unstable: whether their 10000-level nesting overflows too depends on how far JavaScriptCore has compiled the wasm by then (its tiers' frames differ in size). When json overflows, it loses its connection at its first nesting test and the backend restarts; when it does not, json and jsonb report the unterminated input instead of 'stack depth limit exceeded', and their to_tsvector tests then fail on dict_snowball.so, because without the restart object_address's failed dlopen still breaks every later one (see dynamic-loading).
